source.title: Attention Smoothing Is All You Need For Unlearning
source.authors: S. Z. Zade; Xiang-Yu Zhou; Si-Jia Liu; Dong-Xiao Zhu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the supplied text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates unlearning outcomes and retained utility using a new attention-smoothing method, but does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The WMDP results report post-unlearning accuracy and MMLU utility for ASU and RMU. These assess forgetting and utility, not whether attacks recover knowledge. The reported TOFU, MUSE, and case-study results likewise do not apply recovery attacks; cited attack findings are not the paper's own results.
record.test_reason: A new unlearning method (ASU) is scored on the WMDP QA and MMLU measures against RMU. These scores bear on the forgetting-with-utility half of version A. No recovery attack (fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, prompting) is run, so B–F and A's robustness half are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that attention-smoothing self-distillation erases targeted facts with coherent outputs and minimal utility loss across TOFU, MUSE and WMDP. On WMDP specifically, they claim ASU is comparable to RMU in forgetting, with similar or slightly better utility. They do not evaluate robustness to recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: ASU trains a student to match a fixed attention-smoothed teacher on forget-set data, with a retain loss; it is not a fine-tuning recovery attack or a reproduction of the original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attention temperature and which layers are smoothed affect the teacher's token-level behavior; the paper reports temperature and layer ablations, not recovery-attack outcomes.
record.problems: The WMDP table gives no uncertainty estimates or chance-level reference. The paper does not evaluate post-unlearning recovery attacks, so the results cannot establish whether knowledge was removed or merely made inaccessible.
record.rows_left_out: TOFU, MUSE, and other WMDP baseline results are not separately extracted because the claim-relevant WMDP comparison is represented by the reported ASU and RMU scores; none of these evaluations tests recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge after ASU or RMU; no attack of any kind is run.
Relearning or fine-tuning attacks: not run.
Direction ablation, or any analysis of whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted: not run.
Quantization of unlearned weights: not run.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context recovery: not run.
ASU is described as 'robust unlearning', but no resistance to any recovery attack is tested.

missing.what: Baselines LLMU, SCRUB and SSD on Zephyr: WMDP Bio 59.5/43.8/50.2, Cyber 39.5/39.3/35.0, MMLU 44.7/51.2/40.7

MUSE News: ASU KnowMem on the forget set is 46.8–48.0, versus 32.8 for the retrain reference and 64.4 for the base model. Knowledge is only partly removed on News; Books results are closer to retrain.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T2: a new method aimed at the forgetting-plus-utility question. The RMU comparator rows effectively replicate the WMDP original's RMU result with the same measure. The record's cannot_determine states were changed: WMDP's 4-choice format gives a ~25% chance level, though the paper does not state it. The introduction argues that gibberish outputs 'may still permit the extraction' of forgotten information, but no extraction test is reported. TOFU forget-efficacy composites have no chance anchor and were not linked to A.

versions.untested_parts: Recovery after unlearning by attacks; whether any reported post-unlearning score is near chance (no chance level is stated).
Fine-tuning or relearning attacks after unlearning.
Ablating an activation direction or testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information after unlearning.
Resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.notes: All 12 rows match Table 7 (App. F). Code is stated as on GitHub, so the record's code=n is likely wrong. Non-RMU baselines ran on Zephyr only. MUSE PrivLeak uses a Min-K% membership test, not a recovery attack. Zephyr RMU 31.2/28.2 equal the WMDP paper's own figures (outside knowledge), so the run may not be independent.

statements.correction: RMU at unlearn layer 7 (MLPs of layers 5–7 updated), zero-shot WMDP MCQ. Zephyr-7B-β: Bio 64.3→31.2, Cyber 44.8→28.2, MMLU 58.5→57.0. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2: Bio 65.1→30.7, Cyber 41.5→32.3, MMLU 59.0→57.7. No attack run; the chance level is not stated.
statements.problem: The statement cites this study's RMU MMLU rows r6/r12, which fit 'MMLU within about 0–4 points'. But the study is missing from 'why', and the only WMDP range given for RMU on Zephyr/Mistral at early layers is 24–29%. Three of this study's four RMU WMDP values (Bio 31.2, 30.7; Mistral Cyber 32.3) fall above that range. Only Zephyr Cyber 28.2 is inside it.

statements.correction: ASU (ICLR 2026; controls; capability check; code stated as on GitHub). Zephyr-7B-β: Bio 64.3→32.1, Cyber 44.8→31.7, MMLU 58.5→57.5. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2: Bio 65.1→31.5, Cyber 41.5→29.5, MMLU 59.0→57.2. Zero-shot WMDP MCQ, no recovery attack. Either name ASU with these values or drop the citation.
statements.problem: The statement cites ASU rows r1/r3 but names only OBLIVIATE, ELM, PINT and TRACE ('all four report their own proposed methods'). None of its numbers come from this study. ASU's Zephyr Bio 32.1 and MMLU drop of 1.0 fall outside the OBLIVIATE ranges (24.3–31.9; down 2.0–3.9) they sit beside. The rows do support the thrust: near-chance WMDP, MMLU kept, no attack.
